children: The Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) said on Thursday that it adjusted its portfolio last year, reallocating investments across equities, private assets, financial alternatives and fixed income, while cutting exposure to real estate.
ADIA, one of the world's largest sovereign wealth funds, is the oldest of Abu Dhabi's three major government-controlled funds that invests on behalf of the emirate's government.

Allocations to private equity increased to 15%-20% from 12%-17% earlier, while financial alternatives increased to 7%-12% from 5%-10%. Meanwhile, investments in real estate fell to 2%-7% from 5%-10% previously.

"Absolute exposure to real estate remained steady, and it remains an important component of the total portfolio offering attractive risk-adjusted returns," said ADIA Managing Director Sheikh Hamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who is also a member of Abu Dhabi's ruling family.
Tariff wars and geopolitical uncertainty rattled global markets throughout 2025, but equities remained resilient, supported by the artificial intelligence boom.

"While this (AI) wave of innovation unlocks significant value, the pace at which new technologies are being adopted means that business models across a variety of sectors may face fundamental disruption with increasing frequency," Sheikh Hamed said, adding that the economic landscape looks susceptible to fluctuations in sentiment and policy in 2026 and beyond.
The fund's 20-year and 30-year annualised rates of return on a point-to-point basis were 6.6% and 7.2% in 2025, respectively, compared with 6.3% and 7.1% in 2024.
"In public market portfolios, ADIA increased allocations to systematic and absolute-return strategies to enhance its risk-adjusted returns and manage periodic bouts of volatility," Sheikh Hamed said.
